messages:
DeployBot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected — elevated GPU error rate in eu-west (alert id: 4729). metric: cuda.error.count spiking from 0.2% -> 8%

Erica (oncall): I'm seeing continuous node flaps on eu-west-gpu-pool-3, started ~08:12 UTC. Affected pods crash with container exit code 139 and kernel logs show CUDA address faults. Rolling restarts started automatically.

Erica (oncall): quick dmesg excerpt from node eu-west-gpu-03:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.678902] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 65, pid=2145, Xid 65: 0a(0x3f)
[ 12345.678904] kernel: BUG: bad access at addr 0x7fffb3e1a000
[ 12345.678905] kernel: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at virtual address 0000000000000008
```

Sam (SRE): copying logs. Do we have a recent runtime change? any new kernel modules or driver rollouts in eu-west in last 6h?

Matt (Runtime Eng): we did roll a model loader hotfix earlier (deploy 7a2b9c) that touched page alignment logic in the NVMe streamer. It only touched user-side alignment checks but could change prefetch alignment patterns. I'm going to check the loader diff.

Matt (Runtime Eng): suspect: a race between KV cache prefetch and device DMA setup causing misaligned addresses hitting the kernel path. Repro steps I want to try: run a small reproducer with high-concurrency batch on the same model and enable memcheck.

Erica (oncall): mitigation proposals (trying in this order):
- reduce batch size to 1 for eu-west inference deployment
- set routing fallback to CPU for non-critical traffic in eu-west
- roll back deploy 7a2b9c if quick revert is safe
- enable extra kube eviction backoff to avoid thundering restarts

Erica (oncall): commands I'm running now:
```sh
kubectl set env deployment/inference -n prod BATCH_SIZE=1 --context=eu-west
infractl routing set-fallback --region eu-west --policy cpu-fallback --reason "cuda address faults"
```

Jules (CS): customer impact — early sampling shows Customer-Z (finance-pro) experienced ~12% request failures; Customer-Y (analytics) saw degraded latency but not full failures. I've opened CS ticket CS-993 and notified both PMs.

Sam (SRE): confirmed: we see a correlated spike in OOM/container-exit-139 events and Xid 65/79 patterns in dmesg. Reverting 7a2b9c would require a canary rollback because it touched the streaming path; prefer short mitigations first.

Matt (Runtime Eng): attempting a targeted reproduce on a staging node with same driver (NVIDIA 525.xx) and memcheck flags. If memcheck shows misaligned DMA, we can produce a minimal repro to share with driver vendor.

Erica (oncall): rolling routing fallback now, and temporarily moving non-paying test traffic to west-eu-legacy cluster. Also increasing autoscaler cooldown to reduce noisy restarts.

Erica (oncall): status update -> error-rate down to ~1.5% after routing fallback and batch size change. still seeing 1-2 kernel faults/hour on specific physical hosts.

Sam (SRE): ack. I'll pick this up for the night. plan: 1) cordon + repro on one impacted host, 2) collect full kernel oops + vmcore if we can, 3) coordinate with driver vendor if memcheck repro succeeds.

Matt (Runtime Eng): note to folks: if we collect vmcore please capture the full GPU state and the process that triggered the fault (pid/comm). cuda-memcheck is noisy but gives useful backtraces for access patterns. Example run:
```sh
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 cuda-memcheck --tool memcheck ./repro_binary --concurrency 32 --seq-len 1024
```

Jules (CS): flagged impacted customers + posted a status update to the portal. CS-993 includes a short summary and the workaround (route to other region / CPU fallback).

Erica (oncall): handing off to Sam for overnight follow-up. If the fault rate climbs above 5 events/hour or customer impact expands, please escalate to Eng Leadership and open an incident SEV.

Sam (SRE): taking handoff — I'll stay on until 04:00 UTC and coordinate next steps. tagging @oncall-next for morning wakeup.

PagerDuty Bot: Hand-off recorded. New oncall: Sam (SRE). Handoff length: 8h.

Sam (SRE): final note: we'll avoid broad cluster-wide reboots unless we have a reproducible trigger. keeping the rollback as last resort. will push logs and memcheck artifacts to the incident folder: /incidents/2245012345/artifacts

Erica (oncall): thanks — :thumbsup: update thread if anything changes.
